column1: # Which clauses are in scope for a changed file — discovery, not a gate.
# globs is a semicolon-separated list of case-pattern globs in the exact
# syntax tools/lib/ratchet.sh's ratchet_glob_matches() already uses for
# not filename expansion, so a bare `*` is not restricted to one path
# segment). A pattern with no `/` therefore matches at any depth — `*.ts`
# matches both `app.ts` and `packages/foo/app.ts` — so most rows need no
# leading `**/`. A literal root filename (`package.json`) matches only the
# repo-root copy; pair it with `*/package.json` to also catch a nested one.
# `*` alone as the entire glob list means "matches every path" and is used
# only where the clause's own doc states, or an existing gate script's
# ratchet_scope_files() pattern proves, that the clause is not file-scoped —
# never as a stand-in for "not sure".
#   [gate]     the exact ratchet_scope_files() pattern a real tools/*.sh gate
#              already uses — copied from source, not guessed
#   [doc]      the clause's own doc names this location or file directly
#   [fleet]    inferred from a naming convention evidenced elsewhere in this
#              `src/`), but not asserted by the clause's own doc
#   [none]     the doc states, or implies by giving no path/language/
#              directory signal at all, that the clause is not file-scoped
# A [fleet] row is the weakest kind here and the one most likely to need
# correction once this ships against a real diff from outside this repo —
# see the PR description for the full list of what could not be grounded
# in a doc or a script.
